evidence.claim: Morgan Stanley / Counterpoint Global argues that AI investment opportunities may include second-order beneficiaries and companies using AI, not only suppliers that build AI technology.
evidence.source_title: AI Beneficiaries: Investing in Second-Order Effects | Morgan Stanley

evidence.claim: Eaton Vance / Counterpoint Global states that the market often focuses on AI enablers such as chipmakers, data centers, and infrastructure providers, while downstream adopters and second-order effects may also create material value.
evidence.source_title: AI's hidden winners: Seeking opportunity beyond the obvious

evidence.claim: Eaton Vance / Counterpoint Global reports that automating half of the roles most susceptible to automation could unlock up to 16% profit-pool expansion for the most adaptive companies, affect 1.7 million roles, and represent $207 billion of potential labor-cost savings.
evidence.source_title: AI's hidden winners: Seeking opportunity beyond the obvious

evidence.claim: External source describes advanced AI chip substrates as becoming more complex across generations, with more layers, larger body sizes, finer features, and embedded power components.
evidence.source_title: Ibiden: The Hidden Bottleneck Beneath AI - Nikhs

evidence.claim: External source claims that as AI substrate complexity increases, the number of suppliers able to manufacture advanced substrates at commercial yields shrinks, reinforcing incumbent yield-learning advantages.
evidence.source_title: Ibiden: The Hidden Bottleneck Beneath AI - Nikhs

evidence.claim: External source argues that AI infrastructure bottlenecks may shift from GPUs and memory toward networking, optical connectivity, high-speed switches, and rack-scale infrastructure.
evidence.source_title: Celestica: AI's Bottleneck Is Shifting - And Market Hasn't Caught Up

evidence.claim: A 2023 supply-chain study describes the lowest capacity among complementary suppliers as the effective capacity and bottleneck that determines supply-chain throughput.
evidence.source_title: Supplier bottleneck and information dissemination - Li - 2023

summary: Layer 2B maps a candidate chunk around AI-server board-level passive components, MLCC dielectric materials, and second-order component distribution signals. Samsung Electro-Mechanics is treated as the reference MLCC leader in this chunk. Vishay, Nippon Chemical Industrial, and Shandong Sinocera remain speculative-shadow candidates because their direct AI-server-grade MLCC or dielectric-powder exposure is not yet proven by the provided evidence. Arrow and Avnet are underfollowed second-order distribution nodes that may provide lead-time, allocation, backlog, and pricing signals if AI-server passive-component tightness emerges. No buy/sell recommendation is made.
